title: Théorie arithmétique. Théorie de Galois des motifs (1965) : notes manuscites (s.d.), tapuscrit (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
§2 opens a definition of a 'CM-structure' on a pair of fields (E, K). The next page calls it a 'structure de Sh.-Tan.' (Shimura–Taniyama). It serves as the combinatorial datum of CM theory (CM type together with its reflex) inside the 1965 'Théorie de Galois des motifs'.

(1) First attempt (top of page).
- Setup: E and K are extensions of Q. 𝔄 is an ideal of E⊗_Q K = E_K, an étale K-algebra (a product of fields when E is finite). K̄ is an algebraic closure of K.
- Extending scalars, 𝔄 generates an ideal 𝔄' of E⊗_Q K̄ = E_K⊗_K K̄. This 𝔄' amounts to a subset Σ ⊂ Spec E_{K̄} ≅ Hom_alg(E, K̄).
- Condition: for every 'conjugation' τ (involution) in G = Gal(K̄/K), τ(Σ) = Hom(E,K̄) − Σ.
- Grothendieck notes that gτg⁻¹ is again a conjugation. Hence τ⁻¹gτg⁻¹ fixes Σ, so Σ is invariant under the closed normal subgroup H generated by these elements. The field of definition K_0 (annotated '= k_Σ', i.e. a reflex-type field) is then forced to be non-real, since τΣ ≠ Σ; otherwise Hom(E,K̄) would be empty.
- He breaks off here. The reason (see Errors) is that this version is degenerate.

(2) Second formulation, with K finite over Q.
- Fix Q̄ and G = Gal(Q̄/Q). E and K correspond to homogeneous G-sets I_E = Hom(E,Q̄) and I_K = Hom(K,Q̄).
- An ideal 𝔄 of E⊗K is the same as a G-invariant (closed) subset Σ ⊂ I_E × I_K. Write Σ' for its complement.
- Choose an embedding K ⊂ Q̄. This gives an origin y ∈ I_K and I_K ≅ G/Q, where Q is the stabiliser of K (not the rationals).
- Set Σ_y = Σ ∩ (I_E × y). The hypothesis is (τ×1)Σ_y = Σ'_y, i.e. (τ×1)Σ_y ⊂ I_E − Σ_y, for complex conjugations τ ∈ G.

(3) Next page.
- The condition is independent of y, because Σ_{gy} = (g×g)Σ_y and conjugations form a conjugacy class. So it reads (τ×1)Σ = Σ' for all conjugations τ.
- Since (τ×τ)Σ = Σ, this is equivalent to (1×τ)Σ = Σ'. So the notion is symmetric in E and K.
- Further claims: it is stable under enlarging E and K, and there is a field of definition K_0.

Modern reading.
- If E is a CM field with CM type Φ and K ⊃ the Galois closure, take Σ = {(φ,ψ) : ψ⁻¹∘φ ∈ Φ}, suitably normalised. The axiom then encodes Φ ⊔ ιΦ = Hom(E,C).
- The symmetry (1×τ) encodes the reflex type, so the datum packages CM type and reflex symmetrically.
- The ideal 𝔄 ⊂ E⊗K is essentially the annihilator, or kernel of the E⊗K-action, on Lie(A) (equivalently gr_F of H¹_dR) of a CM abelian variety or CM motive over K with multiplication by E.
- The axiom forces E (and, by symmetry, K) to be totally imaginary. It forces the field of definition into the field fixed by the group generated by products of two conjugations, i.e. into a CM field.
errors: The first definition is degenerate, and the page itself half-notices this. 𝔄 is an ideal of E⊗K, so Σ ⊂ Hom(E,K̄) is automatically Gal(K̄/K)-invariant. Hence τΣ = Σ for every conjugation τ ∈ Gal(K̄/K), which contradicts τΣ = complement unless Hom(E,K̄) is empty. So if K has a real place no CM-structure exists, and if K is totally imaginary the condition is vacuous. This explains the abrupt switch to the second formulation, where τ ranges over conjugations in Gal(Q̄/Q) acting on the E-factor only.

The relative notion 'K_0 = field of definition is non-real' is stated loosely. In the corrected formulation the precise statement is that the field of definition lies in the fixed field of the subgroup generated by products cc' of conjugations, i.e. in a CM field (or Q). This is completed only on the next page, in struck-out text.
Minor: 'conjugaison' is used without definition. It should mean the conjugates in G of complex conjugation, i.e. elements of order 2 (Artin–Schreier).

ideas.what: CM-structure on a pair (E,K) as an ideal of E⊗_Q K, equivalently a G-invariant Σ ⊂ Hom(E,Q̄)×Hom(K,Q̄) with (τ×1)Σ = complement for all conjugations τ
ideas.modern_name: CM type with values in K / Shimura–Taniyama datum; type of a CM motive (Hodge/Lie-algebra type as E⊗K-module)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Shimura–Taniyama (1961) for CM types; formulations via E⊗K-modules in Deligne, Milne and others

ideas.what: Symmetry of the condition in E and K via (τ×τ)Σ = Σ, so (τ×1)Σ = Σ' iff (1×τ)Σ = Σ'
Σ invariant under the closed normal subgroup generated by τ⁻¹gτg⁻¹, so the field of definition (reflex-type field k_Σ) is non-real and contained in a CM field
ideas.modern_name: reflex field lies in the maximal CM field Q^cm; CM types induced from CM subfields

ideas.what: Translating ideals of E⊗K into G-invariant subsets of products of homogeneous G-sets (Galois-theoretic dictionary for étale algebras)
ideas.modern_name: Grothendieck's Galois theory: finite étale algebras ↔ finite G-sets

missed.claim: Grothendieck (c.1965) formulates CM types and their reflexes as a single symmetric object: an ideal of E⊗_Q K, i.e. a correspondence Σ ⊂ I_E×I_K. He names it a 'Shimura–Taniyama structure' and treats it inside his motivic Galois theory notes. This is a mild conceptual variant of known material rather than a new result. It does document early engagement with CM motives and Shimura–Taniyama theory inside the motivic Galois program, predating the Taniyama group (Langlands, Deligne, 1979).
missed.quote: On dit que 𝔄 définit une CM-structure sur E, relativement à K, si l'idéal 𝔄' de E⊗K̄ ... τ(Σ)=(Spec E_K̄)−Σ
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical: it shows CM motives and reflex data were being built into the 'théorie de Galois des motifs' in 1965. The symmetric correspondence form is convenient for CM motives with coefficients, but mathematically it is equivalent to standard CM-type/reflex theory.

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics (CM types, reflex duality, reflex field in a CM field) is classical Shimura–Taniyama theory. The symmetric 'ideal of E⊗K' packaging is neat and historically interesting as part of 1965 motivic Galois theory, but would not surprise a specialist. The first definition is degenerate and is abandoned on the page.
transcription_corrections: 'Q' in 'I_K ≃ G/Q' and 'Q sous-groupe de G qui laisse fixe les éléments de K' is a subgroup (stabiliser of K), not the rationals.

The annotation next to K_0 reads '= k_Σ'. The underlined word after 'le corps K_0 est' is hard to read; it is probably a qualifier like 'non réel' or a CM-type adjective, and the transcription's '\underline{non-réel}[?]' is uncertain.
The bracketed remark should read '[puisque sinon on aurait Spec E_K̄ = ∅, ce qui n'est pas]'.
'E⊗_Q K̄*' is probably 'E⊗_Q K̄' with a stray mark; the right side is E_K⊗_K K̄.
Top-left marginal note is only partly legible; it likely refers to 'Σ ⊂ ... de E⊗K' (the subset defined by the ideal of E⊗K).
